title: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud
hook: the shepherd boy who became one of the great reciters (Bukhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday, Ja'far, who took up the banner at Mu'tah and was called the one with two wings. Your line was: two wings. Which duty did you hold on to all day? Day eight hundred thirty-two.

Recite to me. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, says it to one of his companions, and the man is startled. Recite to you? he asks. When it was revealed to you? The Prophet answers: I love to hear it from someone else. So the man opens his mouth and begins. The one being asked is not a chief or a merchant. He is a man who once, tradition says, looked after other people's sheep outside Mecca. Today: Ibn Mas'ud.
screen: `RECITE TO ME.` → `WHEN IT CAME TO YOU?` → `I LOVE TO HEAR IT FROM ANOTHER.`

segments.voice: Start with the hillside. A story in Musnad Ahmad tells that young Abdullah was tending a flock for one of the Meccan chiefs when the Prophet and Abu Bakr passed by and asked for milk. He said the sheep were not his to give. Hold on to that honesty; it is where the story begins. He became Muslim, and he stayed close to the Prophet, and he learned the Qur'an straight from his mouth. Sahih al-Bukhari records the Prophet naming the people to learn the Qur'an from, and Abdullah ibn Mas'ud is named in that short list. Ibn Mas'ud himself says, also in Bukhari, that there was no surah he did not know where it was revealed, and that if he knew anyone who knew the book better and could be reached by camel, he would ride to him. Sure of what he knew, and still hungry to learn more, in the same breath. Now back to the hook. When the Prophet asks him to recite, Bukhari says, he begins Surat an-Nisa. He reaches the verse that asks how it will be when a witness is brought from every people, and the Prophet brought as a witness over them. And the Prophet says: enough. Ibn Mas'ud looks up, and the Prophet's eyes are streaming with tears. The shepherd boy's voice carried the words, and the one who first received them wept to hear them from someone else. Not a voice on show. The text, carried until it landed.
screen: `A SHEPHERD WHO WOULDN'T GIVE AWAY MILK.` · `ONE OF THE NAMES TO LEARN FROM.` · `HE BEGINS SURAT AN-NISA.` · `ENOUGH, WITH TEARS.` · then, large: `THE SHEPHERD RECITER.`

segments.voice: The practice: recite one surah beautifully. Settle, and breathe. Choose a short surah you know, or one line of any text you love. If you know al-Fatiha or al-Ikhlas, that is enough. Say it slowly, under your breath or aloud. Give each word its full length. Let the pauses be pauses. Don't rush to the end. If you don't recite, you can simply listen to a recording of a single short surah, or sit with one line in your mind and hear it said well. Notice what changes when it is said carefully. The bell holds the time.
Ibn Mas'ud, the one-time shepherd who learned the Qur'an from the Prophet's own mouth, was named as a teacher of it, and recited until the Prophet wept. Today's word.
Your line: the shepherd reciter. Today, say one thing you love slowly and well, as if someone is listening closely. Day eight hundred thirty-two.

howItsDone: Muslims learn about Abdullah ibn Mas'ud as a teacher of the Qur'an, and retell the hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari where the Prophet asked him to recite and wept at Surat an-Nisa.

fork.setup: you are a young shepherd outside Mecca. two travelers ask you for milk from the flock you are tending for someone else. what do you say?
options: give them milk; no one will notice.
say the sheep are not yours to give.
fork.reveal: in the story told in Musnad Ahmad, the boy said the sheep were not his. the travelers were the Prophet and Abu Bakr.

original.note: Arabic: 'recitation', reading the Qur'an aloud; from the same root as Qur'an.

trapdoor: what you thought: the Prophet recited and the companions listened.
what it means: he also asked others to recite to him, and wept listening to Ibn Mas'ud.
what a scholar hears: Bukhari's report stops at the verse of the witness in Surat an-Nisa, verse 41.

notes: Audit: 'Proud, and hungry to learn more' could read as calling a revered companion arrogant; changed to 'Sure of what he knew, and still hungry to learn more'.
Index hook cites Bukhari; the shepherd story is in Musnad Ahmad (not Bukhari), attributed accordingly. In Ahmad's version the Prophet then milks a ewe that had not borne young; left out. Confirm.
Bukhari 3758 names four; the script says 'a short list' without the count. Confirm.
Hadith numbers cited from memory; confirm.
